messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [AUTO] capacity-tier-routing: spike in 5xx and misroutes detected for tenant=acme-inc (hosted -> dedicated). Threshold breached: error_rate=12.4% (>5%). Routing fallback activity high from 10:23:11 -> 10:28:32 UTC.
Maria Chen: seeing a bunch of customer tickets from Acme. They report timeouts and degraded responses. Can someone pick this up?
Lauren (Product): Acme says degraded UX on their chat widget; they see 'model unavailable' errors. High priority, they have an active launch.
Ashok Patel: I'm on it. Looking at router logs now. Initial hypothesis: fallback policy is sending production tenant traffic to dedicated pool that is exhausted, causing queue timeouts and 5xx.
Sam (SRE): paging. @ops-tim are you on-call for dedicated pools? If not I'll take.
ops-tim: I'm on-call for infra, but dedicated pool ops are with Sam. Paging @Sam (SRE).
Infra Pager: @Sam (SRE) accepted the page.
Sam (SRE): picking up. Can we mute noisy alerts and surface the per-tenant errors only?
incident-bot: Alerts muted for routing-anomaly:1775001234 by Sam (SRE).
Ashok Patel: quick triage — I pulled a sample of the routing decisions around 10:24. The fallback-policy evaluation order appears to have been reordered after yesterday's deploy to routing-service. Example decision trace:
```
route_request { tenant: "acme-inc", region_hint: "us-west-2", tier: "hosted", model_pref: "redwood-l-lite" }
policy_eval: allow-hosted -> false
policy_eval: fallback-to-dedicated -> true (matched global-fallback regex)
policy_action: route -> dedicated_pool:d-43
```
Ashok Patel: The problematic bit is global-fallback regex '.*prod.*' in the policy that was intended to match env tags, but because tenant metadata includes an internal tag 'organization-prod-legacy' it accidentally matched acme's tenant id. So acme got classified into fallback path.
Maria Chen: who changed that regex?
Sam (SRE): looks like last commit 2026-03-14 by frank-router in routing-configs. There's a PR where priority got flipped for global fallbacks.
ops-tim: dedicated pool d-43 shows queue depth spike and preemption of tenant isolation — dedicated capacity tried to accept but preemption policy didn't isolate because tenant isolation ACL didn't attach (race in pool assignment).
Lauren (Product): impact estimate from support: ~1200 requests failed across multiple users in Acme between 10:23 and 10:29. No data exfiltration, just availability.
Ashok Patel: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) disable global fallback policy rule 'global-fallback-regex' 2) pin acme-inc to hosted routing with an ACL 3) temporarily scale d-43 or divert new requests to warm spare pools.
Sam (SRE): doing step 1 now — disabling fallback rule.
Sam (SRE): CLI: `redwoodctl routing update-policy global-fallback-regex --state disabled` -> accepted.
incident-bot: Policy global-fallback-regex changed to disabled by Sam (SRE) at 10:31:07 UTC.
Ashok Patel: applying tenant pin for acme-inc: `redwoodctl tenants pin acme-inc --route hosted --reason "isolation after misroute"`
Sam (SRE): pinned. Confirmed new requests from acme are hitting hosted pool and 200s returning.
ops-tim: scaling dedicated pool d-43 by +2 GPUs to drain queued work: `infractl scale pool d-43 --gpu 2` — started.
Maria Chen: support: letting Acme know we rolled back fallback rule and pinned them. Sending short incident note.
Lauren (Product): customer message draft: "We experienced a routing issue that briefly affected your requests. We have isolated your traffic and reverted the fallback rule. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a postmortem."
Ashok Patel: root cause notes so far: 1) routing config change reordered policy evaluation 2) overly broad regex matched tenant metadata 3) tenant isolation did not attach because pool assignment race triggered preemption path 4) monitoring lacked a per-tenant fallback alert to catch this earlier.
Sam (SRE): recommended next steps: revert the policy reorder change (hotfix), add a deploy-time lint to prevent regexes that match tenant IDs, add a gating alert: per-tenant fallback >0.5% in 5m.
ops-tim: I've enabled an emergency ACL on dedicated pools to reject cross-tenant fallbacks temporarily.
incident-bot: Fallback rejections enabled for dedicated pools by ops-tim.
Maria Chen: support reports Acme's errors dropped to near zero within ~2 minutes of the pin. Good.
Lauren (Product): request to prioritize postmortem and customer follow-up. Also need communication schedule: 1) initial note (sent), 2) follow-up within 24h with root cause and ETA for fix, 3) postmortem within 72h.
Sam (SRE): handing off to Ashok for remediation and rollback verification. I'm going to sleep on-call but available for escalations.
Ashok Patel: taking handoff. My contact: ashok.patel@redwood.ai. Will track remediation and PR to fix regex + guardrails.
ops-tim: making a runbook entry for emergency pin and pool ACLs: `docs/runbooks/tenant-misroute-isolation.md` (drafted).
incident-bot: Incident severity -> Sev2 (partial outage for single customer). Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0423-77.
Maria Chen: add postmortem owners: Ashok (eng-routing), Sam (sre), Lauren (product comms).
Sam (SRE): final note: watch for related anomalies in eu-west-1 — there was a similar config drift earlier but suppressed. I'll run a config-diff sweep tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: thanks everyone. Closing Slack thread once postmortem ticket created and customer notified.
ops-tim: :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Thread closed by Maria Chen at 10:48:10 UTC (created incident ticket INC-2026-0423-77).
